exactText: I believe that, within the next decade, we will not only get the world back on track but enter a new era of unprecedented progress.
sourceQuote: within the next decade, we will not only get the world back on track but enter a new era of unprecedented progress.
normalizedClaim: Within the next decade (by ~2036) the world will get back on track and enter a new era of unprecedented progress.
resolutionCriteria: Major global indicators (poverty rates, child mortality, disease burden, clean energy deployment per World Bank/WHO/IEA data) showing substantial improvement and accelerated progress by 2036 relative to mid-2020s baselines.

exactText: There is no upper limit on how intelligent AIs will get or on how good robots will get, and I believe the advances will not plateau before exceeding human levels.
sourceQuote: the advances will not plateau before exceeding human levels.
normalizedClaim: AI and robot capabilities will not plateau before exceeding human-level performance across a broad range of tasks.
resolutionCriteria: Consensus among major AI labs and independent benchmarks showing AI systems exceeding top human performance on a majority of economically and cognitively relevant tasks, without clear plateau, by 2035.

exactText: The bioterrorism risk is 50 times the natural pandemic risk now.
sourceQuote: The bioterrorism risk is 50 times the natural pandemic risk now.
normalizedClaim: The risk of AI-enabled bioterrorism is currently approximately 50 times higher than the risk of a natural pandemic.
resolutionCriteria: Expert risk assessments from biosecurity organizations (e.g., Johns Hopkins, WHO, or independent panels) quantifying relative likelihood of AI-assisted vs natural pandemic threats around 2026–2030.

exactText: Using AI, we will soon be able to provide poor farmers with better advice about weather, prices, crop diseases, and soil than even the richest farmers get today.
sourceQuote: we will soon be able to provide poor farmers with better advice about weather, prices, crop diseases, and soil than even the richest farmers get today.
normalizedClaim: AI systems will soon deliver superior agronomic advice to poor farmers compared with what the richest farmers currently receive.
resolutionCriteria: Deployment and independent evaluation of AI farming advisory tools in low-income countries demonstrating higher-quality recommendations than baseline high-income farmer practices, documented by Gates Foundation reports or peer-reviewed studies by 2030.

exactText: my view is it’s only a couple of years [until robots compete in physical jobs].
sourceQuote: it’s only a couple of years
normalizedClaim: Robots capable of competing with humans in physical jobs (construction, hospitality, etc.) will arrive within a couple of years (by ~2028–2029).
resolutionCriteria: Commercial deployment of humanoid or specialized robots performing economically relevant physical labor at scale in industries such as construction or hospitality, reported by major manufacturers or labor statistics by 2029.

exactText: With the right investments and policies in place, over the next ten years we will have new affordable zero-carbon technologies ready to roll out at scale.
sourceQuote: over the next ten years we will have new affordable zero-carbon technologies ready to roll out at scale.
normalizedClaim: By ~2035, new affordable zero-carbon technologies (especially for hard-to-abate sectors) will be ready for large-scale deployment.
resolutionCriteria: Commercial availability and cost-competitiveness of zero-carbon solutions for steel, cement, aviation, or similar sectors, as tracked by IEA or Breakthrough Energy reports by 2035.

exactText: I’ll let the temperature go up 0.1 degree to get rid of malaria.
sourceQuote: I’ll let the temperature go up 0.1 degree to get rid of malaria.
normalizedClaim: Eradicating malaria is preferable to preventing an additional 0.1°C of warming if a trade-off must be made.
resolutionCriteria: This is a normative preference statement rather than a falsifiable forecast of events; tracked as a stated priority in Gates Foundation allocation decisions through 2030.
imputationNote: Normative preference rather than a testable forecast; treated as a take with a 2030 review horizon for whether Gates Foundation resource allocation reflects this priority.

exactText: in the majority of occupations, humans will eventually be “vastly inferior to the AI doing the job.”
sourceQuote: humans will eventually be “vastly inferior to the AI doing the job.”
normalizedClaim: In the majority of occupations, AI will eventually perform the work at a level vastly superior to humans.
resolutionCriteria: Labor economics studies and capability benchmarks showing AI outperforming average human workers on core tasks in >50% of major occupational categories by 2035.

exactText: We’re already starting to see the impact of AI on the job market, and I think this impact will grow over the next five years.
sourceQuote: this impact will grow over the next five years.
normalizedClaim: AI’s impact on the job market will increase substantially over the next five years (by 2031).
resolutionCriteria: BLS, OECD, or World Bank labor data showing accelerated job displacement, task automation rates, or unemployment shifts attributable to AI between 2026 and 2031.

exactText: by the middle of this century emissions will be lower and the gap between poor countries and rich countries will be greatly reduced.
sourceQuote: by the middle of this century emissions will be lower and the gap between poor countries and rich countries will be greatly reduced.
normalizedClaim: By ~2050 global emissions will be lower than current levels and the development gap between poor and rich countries will be greatly reduced.
resolutionCriteria: IEA or Global Carbon Project data showing lower global CO₂ emissions in 2050 vs mid-2020s, plus World Bank metrics on income/health gaps between high- and low-income countries narrowing substantially.
